verdict.rationale: Poly documents Flashback, a timeline that rewinds any file or folder to how it looked at a past moment. It also documents restoring any version, rolling back files or folders in a click, undoing a specific change, and restoring conflict revisions. Deletes via rm go to an Archive and are reversible, and notes are Markdown files, so all of this covers notes. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of restore flows, and explicit documentation of the user-facing Archive recovery workflow for deleted notes (only mentioned in MCP context).

support.subject: As a power-user, I can view a note's version history and restore earlier versions or recover deleted notes

citations.quote: Flashback is time travel for your files. Open it and your current view — a folder, a file — gains a timeline of its entire past.
Even conflicting edits are preserved, so you can recover any version of any file at any time.
Rollback your files, or whole folders in a click.
can be opened, peeked, downloaded, or restored like any other version.
rm archives files (reversible), and permanently deleting from the Archive is reserved for you
New journal entries are Markdown files synced to your **Mind** folder.
